The inversion of the upper hinge pin is not an uncommon practice and is intended to prevent a gate from being easily lifted off its hinges. BS 1722-12:2006 specification for steel palisade fences which states that 'hinges shall be designed so that it is impossible to remove the gates by lifting at the hinges when they are in the shut and locked position'. The standard gives examples of hinge arrangements and does not specifically preclude this method.
